h1: The 7 Best HDMI Portable Monitors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best HDMI Portable Monitors: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven 15.6-inch HDMI portable monitors compared on ports, stands, warranty and budget, so you pick the right one.
summary: The KYY 15.6-inch with its magnetic cover is our best all-rounder, while the cocopar adds a full-size HDMI port and VESA mounting. The ASUS ZenScreen wins on warranty, the ARZOPA on a built-in stand, and the MNN is the cheapest way in.
intro: The most common mistake with an HDMI portable monitor is assuming every HDMI port is the same. Several models here use mini-HDMI, which means a cable swap or an adapter before your console or desktop card will connect, and that detail is rarely in the product title.

We reviewed seven 15.6-inch 1080P panels and ranked them on the spec sheet: port type, stand design, mounting options, warranty and price bucket. Every pick supports USB-C and HDMI, so the differences come down to how you plan to plug in and where the screen will sit.

products.name: KYY Portable Monitor 15.6" 1080P Computer Monitor Screen Extender w/Cover
products.verdict: The safest all-rounder for laptops, consoles and travel bags.
products.description:
This KYY is a 15.6-inch 1080P IPS panel with a 178 degree viewing angle, two USB-C ports and a mini-HDMI input. It weighs 1.7 lb and measures 0.3 inch thick, so it slides into a laptop sleeve without fuss.

It ranks first because the magnetic smart cover doubles as the stand, which means nothing extra to carry, and the built-in stereo speakers plus a 3.5mm audio out cover sound too. It gives up the full-size HDMI and VESA holes of the cocopar below, which is the real tradeoff.

Buy it if you want one monitor for a work laptop and an occasional console session and you are happy to use mini-HDMI. Skip it if your source only has a full-size HDMI output and you do not want to buy a cable.
products.idealFor: Travelers who split time between a laptop and a console.
products.skipIf: Your source device only offers full-size HDMI.

products.name: cocopar Portable Monitor 15.6 Inch 1080P FHD 60Hz 85% sRGB Travel Monitor with Speaker HDMI USB-C
products.verdict: A full-size HDMI port and VESA holes make it the flexible desk pick.
products.description:
The cocopar pairs a 15.6-inch 1080P IPS panel covering 85% sRGB with two full-featured USB-C ports and a full-size HDMI port. It weighs 1.5 lb without the cover and is 4mm at its slimmest point.

It sits just under the KYY because it sits in the $100-200 bucket, a step up from the $50-100 picks around it. What you get for the money is VESA mounting through two holes on the back, so it can leave the table and hang on an arm.

Choose it if the screen will live at a desk and you want a standard HDMI cable to plug straight in. Skip it if you only need a travel monitor and would rather spend less.
products.idealFor: Desk users who want to mount the screen on an arm.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest travel screen available.

products.name: UPERFECT Portable Monitor, 15.6" IPS 1920x1080 FHD Eye Care Travel Screen
products.verdict: Standard HDMI plus an OTG port for older laptops and desktop cards.
products.description:
UPERFECT offers a 15.6-inch FHD IPS screen with a flicker-free eye care backlight, a standard full-size HDMI port, dual USB Type-C and an OTG port. It also has a 75x75mm M4 VESA pattern and dual stereo speakers.

It lands below the cocopar because the spec sheet lists fewer color details, but it costs less and keeps the full-size HDMI and VESA support. Against the KYY above it, you trade a little portability for broader port compatibility.

Reach for it when an older laptop, desktop graphics card or console offers only a full-size HDMI socket; the OTG port also takes a wired mouse or keyboard. Skip it if you want the lightest possible travel screen.
products.idealFor: Owners of older laptops or desktop graphics cards.
products.skipIf: Weight is your top priority for travel.

products.name: ASUS ZenScreen 15.6" Portable Monitor for Laptop (MB169CK)
products.verdict: A three-year warranty and a 360 degree kickstand set it apart.
products.description:
The ASUS ZenScreen is a 15.6-inch FHD IPS anti-glare panel with TUV-certified eye care, two USB-C ports and a mini-HDMI input. The 360 degree built-in kickstand and tripod socket give it more setup options than a fold-over cover.

It ranks fourth because it offers fewer ports than UPERFECT and no full-size HDMI, yet the 3-year warranty is the longest on the list. It weighs 0.78kg and is 11.8mm thick.

Pick it if you want the manufacturer backing and a sturdier stand. Skip it if you need a full-size HDMI input without an adapter.
products.idealFor: Buyers who value warranty and a sturdy built-in stand.
products.skipIf: You only have full-size HDMI sources.

products.name: ARZOPA Portable Monitor 15.6'' FHD 1080P - Ultra-Slim with Kickstand
products.verdict: A metal housing and always-attached stand suit frequent console hookups.
products.description:
The ARZOPA is a 15.6-inch 1920x1080 IPS panel in a metal housing with USB-C and HDMI connectivity and a built-in kickstand. It weighs 1.6 lb and is 0.35 inch thick.

It sits below the ASUS because the spec sheet lacks a warranty length or an eye care certification, but its stand is always attached and ready. The listing names PS3, PS4, PS5, Xbox and Switch compatibility.

It fits console players who hook up often and dislike fiddling with a loose cover. Skip it if you want listed mounting holes or extra ports.
products.idealFor: Console players who hook up screens often.
products.skipIf: You want VESA mounting or a long warranty.

products.name: KYY Portable Monitor 15.6'' FHD 1080P USB C HDMI Gaming Monitor Ultra-Slim IPS Display
products.verdict: Everything you need is in the box, including the HDMI cable.
products.description:
This second KYY model is a 15.6-inch 1080P IPS panel with HDR mode and 1000:1 contrast, two USB-C ports and a mini-HDMI input. The box adds a mini-HDMI-to-HDMI cable, two USB-C cables and a screen protector.

It ranks below the first KYY because the body specs match but the stand is a foldable cover with two viewing-angle grooves rather than a magnetic cover that is listed with speakers. The included cables are the reason to consider it.

It suits console gamers who do not want to order a cable separately. Skip it if you already own the cables.
products.idealFor: Console gamers who want a complete kit.
products.skipIf: You already own the cables you need.

products.name: MNN 15.6" FHD 60Hz Portable Monitor USB-C HDMI IPS HDR Gaming Laptop
products.verdict: The lowest price here, with HDR and several display modes.
products.description:
The MNN is a 15.6-inch FHD 60Hz IPS monitor with HDR mode, two full-feature USB-C ports and an HDMI input. It supports copy, extend, second-screen and portrait display modes, and its smart cover doubles as the stand.

It ranks last because it skips VESA mounting and the 3-year warranty of the ASUS, but it is the only pick in the $25-50 bucket, so the savings are real.

It fits budget buyers who want a basic second screen with multiple display modes. Skip it if you want long warranty coverage.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting a basic second screen.
products.skipIf: You want VESA mounting or a long warranty.

whatMatters.detail: Mini-HDMI and full-size HDMI are different connectors, and several monitors here use the smaller one. A mismatch means buying a cable or adapter before you can connect a console or desktop. Check the listing for the words mini-HDMI or full-size HDMI, and confirm the box includes the cable you need.

A smart cover that folds into a stand is light but gives fewer angles, while a built-in kickstand stays attached. This matters if you set the screen up daily. Look for the stand type in the product bullets and whether a tripod socket is listed.
VESA holes let you hang the screen on an arm instead of using table space. Only some picks list them. Check for a pattern such as 75x75mm in the specs before you rely on it.
A portable screen gets packed and unpacked often, so longer coverage is useful. The ASUS lists three years, which is the longest here. Look for a listed warranty length rather than an assumption.
Some boxes include HDMI and USB-C cables, others do not. That can add to the real cost of a cheap monitor. Check the in-the-box list on the listing.

faq.q: Do these work with a laptop over USB-C?
faq.a: All seven list USB-C connectivity, and most have two USB-C ports. Your laptop's port must support video output, so check its spec sheet before buying.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Assuming HDMI means full-size HDMI. The KYY models and the ASUS use mini-HDMI, so you need a mini-to-full cable, which the second KYY includes.

faq.q: Is the ASUS worth it over a cheaper pick?
faq.a: If you value its 3-year warranty, TUV-certified eye care and 360 degree kickstand, yes. If you just want a second screen, the MNN costs less.

faq.q: How do I set one up with a console?
faq.a: Connect the console's HDMI output to the monitor's HDMI input, then power the monitor over USB-C. The ARZOPA and second KYY list console compatibility.

faq.q: How do I keep the screen safe in a bag?
faq.a: Use the included cover or case, and keep it in a laptop sleeve. The KYY models are 0.3 inch thick, so avoid stacking heavy items on them.

faq.q: Can I mount one on a monitor arm?
faq.a: Only if the listing shows VESA holes. The cocopar and UPERFECT list them, and UPERFECT uses a 75x75mm M4 pattern.

finalTake: The KYY with its magnetic cover is the best all-rounder for most people. Move to the cocopar for full-size HDMI and VESA mounting, or the ASUS ZenScreen for the warranty. If money is tight, the MNN is a fair starting point, and check the HDMI port size before you order.
